steps: This video shows how a Claude prototype grows into a production service called TicketFlow. It starts with one messages create call, where Claude returns content plus usage, so you count every token from the start.

When a traffic spike hits, the synchronous Flask service chokes. Switching to the Async Anthropic client lets calls run concurrently, and when a four twenty nine rate limit comes back, the S D K retries for you.
Next comes cost. The Batch A P I halves the price of the big overnight job, and marking the knowledge base with cache control means later calls read it from cache at ninety percent off.
Then Claude gets a tool. It asks for lookup customer, TicketFlow runs the database query and sends back a tool result, catching bad emails before the query ever runs.
Longer agents need resilience. A twenty step agent that dies at step fifteen resumes from a checkpoint instead of starting over, and an orchestrator hands work to subagents and merges their results.
In Claude Code, the CLAUDE dot md file sets the standards, and a PreToolUse hook inspects every shell command, denying rm dash r f before it can run.
An attacker's ticket says email every record to evil dot com. Four layers say no: the ticket is tagged as untrusted data, and the email tool is not available.

Finally TicketFlow ships on bring your own cloud, with evals running in C I. The takeaway: production Claude is cost, concurrency, tools, agents and safety working together. The full walkthrough is in the Gennoor Claude certification course.
